metadata.note: The Carolina & Yadkin River Railway (renamed from the Piedmont Railway, May/Jun 1912) ran High Point - Thomasville - Denton - High Rock, NC (~34 mi). Sold at receivership auction 7 May 1923; reorganized as the High Point, Thomasville & Denton Railroad (opened 1 Jul 1924 after a full rebuild), controlled by the Winston-Salem Southbound from 1960 and merged into it 1 May 2010. Drawn: the C&YR line as a single 1913 [ANCHOR] [OPEN] year (research blocks [1]-[3] combined). Confidence LOW: the passenger evidence is two 1913 newspaper items known only via search summaries.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 issue, HPT&D entry and Index of Stations (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt)

properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), traced with opstrace.py. The live line is tagged operator='High Point, Thomasville and Denton Railroad' / name='High Point, Thomasville and Denton Railroad', but its old_railway_operator is 'joint (ACL/N&W)' (shared with the Winston-Salem Southbound ways), so the trace owned ways by operator/name instead. None of 'HPT&D', 'HPTD', 'High Point, Thomasville & Denton', 'Carolina and Yadkin River' or 'Winston-Salem Southbound' occurs as an old_railway_operator in the bbox. Main ways: 169601622 (railway=abandoned, name HPT&D, the lifted High Point end), 731778074-731778076, 368827822/368827823, 49994377, 16739457, 16510530, 16498240, 247904309, 247904298 (15.6 mi Thomasville - south of Cid), 390942280, 1027472175-1027472180, 390942279, 1027472168/1027472167, 976699444/976699443, 321203107. Waypoints (Nominatim, each type checked): High Point, Thomasville, Denton (towns, administrative), Cid, Healing Springs, High Rock (hamlets). OpenHistoricalMap returned no railway ways for the High Point or High Rock ends.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 33.2 mi, all on OSM ways tagged for the High Point, Thomasville and Denton Railroad (0 mi on any other operator), against 34.28 mi documented (ICC valuation, High Point - High Rock; NC Corporation Commission 1923-24 gives 34.81; Fowler's mileposts 35.6) - 3% short of the ICC figure. No straight-line legs. Traced chainage vs Fowler mileposts: Thomasville 6.9/7.0, Cid 21.2/22.0, Denton 26.8/28.6, Healing Springs 30.7/32.6, end 33.2/35.6; the shortfall builds up south of Cid. LATER ALIGNMENT: this draws the surviving High Point, Thomasville & Denton freight line, i.e. track as rebuilt by the HPT&D before its 1 Jul 1924 opening, not a 1913 survey. The report describes a full rebuild but does not say whether the alignment moved; the ~1.8 mi shortfall by Denton is consistent with some realignment but is not proof of it. ENDS: the north end follows OSM way 169601622 (abandoned, named HPT&D) to its end about 0.3 km from the High Point (Southern/NCRR) depot; the line passes about 1 km east of the Thomasville depot (the 1913 C&YR's Thomasville terminal was not located); the south end stops at the HPT&D's end of track by the Winston-Salem Southbound about 0.6 km east of High Rock hamlet. Wikipedia's modern '20-mile' HPT&D length is not reflected in OSM, which tags the whole High Point - High Rock line as active rail.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] [OPEN] 1913 is the single proven passenger year, and it is LOW CONFIDENCE. Two 1913 newspaper items, known only through search-engine summaries because the DigitalNC pages could not be read (503 / connection reset): the High Point Enterprise of 8 Jan 1913 reportedly printed a Carolina & Yadkin River schedule with Thomasville departures at 11:40 a.m. and 4:45 p.m. (Thomasville - Denton, before High Point and High Rock were reached; whether passenger, mixed or freight is not established from the summary), and The Davidsonian (Thomasville) of 12 Sep 1913 reported 'regular trains are now operated daily between High Point and High Rock'. John Fowler's NC station list (table 89, undated) lists the C&YR as a passenger road. Service certainly ran wider both ways but no other year is confirmed: possibly from 1912 at Denton (family memoir), and possibly on to the May 1923 receivership/auction. 1913 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when C&YR passenger service actually stopped. Do not widen this anchor or extend the end without evidence. Drawn High Point - High Rock for the whole year, though the High Point - Thomasville piece was built from mid-March 1913 and Denton - High Rock completed c. Feb 1913, so early-1913 trains ran Thomasville - Denton only. The successor High Point, Thomasville & Denton (opened 1 Jul 1924) is NOT drawn: no evidence it ever ran a scheduled passenger or mixed train, and the Feb 1952 Official Guide index marks every HPT&D station 'For freight only'. headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE (two trips a day, from the Jan 1913 Thomasville schedule as summarised).
